title: Real-Time Chat
summary: Deliver one-to-one and small group messages in real time with history and receipts.
statement:
Design a chat service for a mobile and web app.

Functional requirements:
- One-to-one conversations and groups of up to 200 members.
- Messages arrive in real time when the recipient is online and are stored for later otherwise.
- Message history is available on every device a user signs in on.
- Sent, delivered, and read indicators, plus online presence.

Scale to assume:
- 100 million daily active users.
- 20 billion messages per day.
- Messages within one conversation must appear in the same order for every member.
hints: How does the server push a message to a phone or browser the moment it arrives? Think about the long-lived connection.
Once you have many connection servers, how does a sender's server find the server holding the recipient's connection?
Pick a storage layout that makes 'load the latest 50 messages of this conversation' cheap.
expectations: Clarifies group size limits, ordering guarantees, multi-device sync, retention, and whether end-to-end encryption is in scope.
Estimates messages per second (hundreds of thousands) and storage per year, and concurrent connections per gateway server.
Uses persistent connections (WebSockets or similar) through a gateway tier, with a session registry mapping users to gateway servers.
Routes messages through a durable queue or log and stores them in a store partitioned by conversation and sorted by time or sequence number.
Assigns per-conversation sequence numbers for ordering and uses client-generated IDs for idempotent retries.
Falls back to mobile push notifications for offline users and syncs missed messages on reconnect using a per-device cursor.
Handles presence with heartbeats and TTLs and discusses the fan-out cost of large groups and read receipts.
